_comment: Departures from the Buerkle spreadsheet. kind "corrected" replaces the source value with "value" (same notation as the spreadsheet); kind "disputed" leaves the source value and flags it. Add an entry only when at least two independent published sources disagree with the source in the unsafe direction, and give the references. conc is the German concentration text of the row, or * for every row of the chemical.

overrides.reason: The resin manufacturer lists PVDF homopolymer as not recommended for sodium hydroxide at every concentration, and two further charts rate it D. The source rates it A to C, mostly as an estimate.

Stainless steel 304 pits in seawater. The Australian Stainless Steel Development Association limits it to fittings that are regularly washed with fresh water, and two charts rate it C. The source rates it A at 20 °C.
Stainless steel 316 is subject to crevice corrosion in seawater above about 10 to 15 °C. The source rates it A at 20 °C.
The British Stainless Steel Association limits 304 to about 5 % sulfuric acid at room temperature; intermediate concentrations corrode it rapidly. The source rates it B.

Neither 304 nor 316 resists sulfuric acid of intermediate concentration: the British Stainless Steel Association limits 304 to about 5 % and 316 to about 22 % at room temperature. The source rates both B.

Neither 304 nor 316 resists sulfuric acid of intermediate concentration: the British Stainless Steel Association limits 304 to about 5 % and 316 to about 22 % at room temperature. The source rates both B.
The INEOS HDPE guide rates methyl ethyl ketone unsatisfactory and two charts rate it D or not recommended for continuous use; one chart rates it resistant.
Published charts disagree: two rate acetone D or not recommended for continuous use on HDPE, while the INEOS HDPE guide rates it satisfactory.
One chart rates methyl isobutyl ketone D on HDPE and the Nalgene table rates it fair.
Two charts that share one data set rate acetal D for dilute hydrogen peroxide. The source itself rates acetal D from 30 %.
Two charts that share one data set rate acetal D for dimethylformamide.
The source value is an estimate. Charts for hydrofluoric acid of 20 % and above, and an O-ring handbook without a stated concentration, rate nitrile rubber unsuitable.
Two charts rate aluminium C and D for dichloromethane.
Two charts rate rigid PVC fair or limited for pure ethanol.
